name: National Museum of the Pacific War
dates: Wednesday through Monday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Pacific Combat Zone closes at 3 p.m.
company: Admiral Nimitz Foundation and Texas Historical Commission
customer: History readers, veterans, families, museum people
unique: A six-acre museum campus devoted to the Pacific Theater, with the Admiral Nimitz Gallery, a Japanese Garden of Peace, combat aircraft and a Pacific Combat Zone with outdoor exhibits.
buzz: The main galleries deserve several hours on their own. Start before lunch so the Pacific Combat Zone does not close before you reach it.

name: Enchanted Rock State Natural Area
cost: $8 age 13 and older, free age 12 and under
dates: Year-round, reserve day passes up to 30 days ahead
unique: A 425-foot pink granite batholith on the Gillespie and Llano county line, with 22 miles of trail, a steep open-rock summit climb, bouldering, caves and dark Hill Country skies.
buzz: Reserve before driving out because the park closes to unreserved visitors at capacity. The Summit Trail has little shade and becomes slick when wet.

name: Luckenbach Texas
cost: Free daytime visit, paid concert prices vary
dates: Open daily, with pickers under the oaks and dances throughout the year
customer: Country music fans, dancers, guitar players, road trippers
unique: An 1849 trading post turned tiny music settlement, where informal picking circles gather beneath old oaks and the dance hall still books Texas country acts.
buzz: A ticketed headliner and an ordinary afternoon picking session are different experiences. Check the calendar, but leave time to sit under the trees with a beer.

name: Pioneer Museum
dates: Monday through Saturday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
customer: Architecture people, genealogists, families, history readers
unique: A 3.5-acre self-guided village explaining Fredericksburg's German settlement through a log cabin, one-room school, barn, smokehouse and an original Sunday house.
buzz: The furnished buildings explain why local houses look the way they do. Sunday houses were small town bases for farm families attending church and trading.

name: Wildseed Farms
cost: Free outside peak bloom, an entry fee applies during peak bloom
dates: Open daily, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., field blooms are seasonal
unique: A working wildflower seed farm with 200 acres at its visitor site, production fields, butterfly gardens and a half-mile accessible trail, plus seeds, plants and estate wine.
buzz: This is a farm rather than a permanent flower display. Check the bloom report before going, and expect a trail entry charge at peak bloom.

name: LBJ Ranch Driving Tour
dates: Daily except Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day, last driving permit at 4 p.m.
customer: Presidential history readers, road trippers, families
unique: A free self-guided route through Lyndon Johnson's working ranch, stopping at his reconstructed birthplace, first school and the Johnson family cemetery, with an official audio tour for the drive.
buzz: Pick up the free permit at the state park visitor center first. The Texas White House, hangar and Jetstar remain closed for rehabilitation, so do not plan around a house tour.

name: Sauer-Beckmann Living History Farm
dates: October through May 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., June through September 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., closed the last Tuesday monthly
customer: Families, cooks, animal people, history readers
unique: Rangers in historical clothing work a World War I era German-Texan farm, feeding animals, milking, cooking on a wood-burning stove, gardening and doing seasonal canning and butchering.
buzz: The appeal is watching work actually happen and asking questions, not just reading labels. Pair it with the adjacent ranch tour, but note that the two sites keep different hours.

name: Becker Vineyards Estate Winery
cost: $27 general tasting, $45 small group tour and tasting
dates: Monday through Thursday 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., Friday and Saturday to 6 p.m., Sunday 11 a.m. to 6 p.m.
customer: Wine people, gardeners, couples, small groups age 21 and up
unique: A working estate with 66 acres of vineyards and a historic German stone barn winery, offering five-sample tastings and guided walks through the production facility and barrel rooms.
buzz: Go to the Becker Farms Road estate rather than the Main Street tasting room if you want to see vineyards and production. Book the small group tour for more than a bar tasting.

name: Vogel Orchard
cost: Produce, ice cream and baked goods priced individually
dates: Seasonal, closed after the 2026 harvest and scheduled to reopen in summer 2027
customer: Fruit growers, road trippers, families, pie people
unique: Three generations of the Vogel family sell local peaches and other seasonal produce from their US 290 orchard stand, alongside preserves, ice cream and peach cobbler.
buzz: Check the crop update before making a special drive. Harvest size and opening days change, and the stand closes completely after the peach season.

name: Old German Bakery and Restaurant
dates: Monday, Tuesday and Friday 7 a.m. to 2 p.m., Saturday and Sunday to 3 p.m., closed Wednesday and Thursday
customer: Breakfast people, bakers, German food fans, families
unique: A family-owned Main Street bakery and breakfast room serving German pancakes, crepes, schnitzel, sausages and breads and pastries baked on site.
buzz: Go early for breakfast and the bakery case. The midweek closure and early afternoon closing time catch visitors who treat it as a dinner option.

name: Gillespie County Fair
cost: 2026 adult grounds admission free Thursday, $15 Friday, $20 Saturday and $10 Sunday
dates: Annual late August, most recently August 27-30, 2026
company: Gillespie County Fair and Festivals Association
customer: Families, horse racing fans, livestock people, fair food fans
unique: Texas's oldest continuous county fair combines pari-mutuel horse racing with livestock judging, household exhibits, a carnival, concerts, washer pitching and a 42 domino tournament.
buzz: Thursday has free grounds and concert admission, while Saturday costs the most. Racing and the 42 tournament give this fair a local character beyond the midway.

name: Albert Icehouse and Dancehall
cost: Many patio and beer garden shows free, dance hall tickets vary
dates: Wednesday through Sunday, with a weekly open pickers circle and regular live shows
customer: Two-steppers, country music fans, guitar players, groups
unique: A century-old 80-by-55-foot dance hall with original hardwood floors anchors a rural icehouse, beer garden and active calendar of dances, concerts and picking circles.
buzz: The Wednesday open pickers circle is an easier participatory stop than a ticketed weekend show. Ticketed dance hall performances are 21 and up, while free patio shows welcome families.

name: Willow City Loop
dates: Daylight hours, wildflower timing varies each spring
customer: Scenic drivers, cyclists, wildflower photographers, geology people
unique: A 13-mile public road looping through private ranch country, limestone hills and creek crossings, known for spring bluebonnets and Indian paintbrush against broad Hill Country views.
buzz: Treat this as a drive or ride, not a park. The surrounding land is private and visitors are discouraged from stopping, parking or walking into the flower fields.

name: Fort Martin Scott State Historic Site
cost: $10 adult, $5 senior and youth, free age 5 and under
dates: Grounds daily 8 a.m. to 8 p.m., site Tuesday through Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
customer: Military history readers, archaeology people, families
unique: The first frontier military post established in Texas after statehood interprets the 1848 to 1853 Army outpost through replica structures and original buildings including the guardhouse and jail.
buzz: The grounds and staffed site keep different hours. Visit during site hours to see the buildings rather than treating the roadside grounds as the whole experience.
